subject: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@swiftframe.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the productive renewal call last week. Per our discussion we pulled together a draft addendum to the MSA that updates the coverage schedule and the capacity uplift rules tied to your Q1 expansion. I attached a tracked-change PDF of the coverage schedule and a doc with the MSA amendments.

Key asks from your side we captured:
- Reduce minimum notice for capacity scale-down to 30 days (you asked for 14; legal flagged risk)
- Explicit backup retention window for cached inference artifacts (30 days vs Redwood default 90)
- SLA credit language for peak concurrency breaches during capacity ramp

Could you confirm whether the priority is (A) earlier retention limits, or (B) shorter scale-down notice? If both, we can propose mitigations in the addendum (e.g., phased scale-down or restricted ramp windows).

Next steps: Marcus will propose concrete redline language after he reviews your comments. If helpful, I can set a 30-minute redline walk-through tomorrow.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: SwiftFrame_CoverageSchedule_redline_v1.pdf, Redwood_MSA_amendment_track_changes.docx
From: Elena Rossi <elena@swiftframe.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@swiftframe.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Two clarifications from our procurement/infra leads:
1) Retention: we really need 30 days for KV/cache artifacts due to our compliance policies for ephemeral PII.
2) Scale-down notice: our product ops team needs 14 days to avoid downstream job failures.

If the 14-day notice is a blocker, can Redwood preserve active allocations for a short-lived grace period (we suggested a one-week buffer) and bill at the reduced reserved rate?

Also: can we get a specific statement about audit support for the private deployment (SOC2 evidence access) in the addendum? We want to avoid separate SOWs.

Happy to join a walk-through. Tomorrow afternoon PST works for Alex + me.

—Elena
Head of Infrastructure, SwiftFrame
elena@swiftframe.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@swiftframe.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T11:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync

Elena —

Thanks — that helps. We heard you on both retention and notice. Quick internal notes:
- 30-day retention is likely acceptable with a privacy carveout; Marcus will confirm exact wording and any dependency on deployment mode (hosted vs private).
- 14-day notice is aggressive for reserved capacity but we can propose a conditional policy: 14-day notice + one-week grace at reduced reserved rate if capacity is not reallocated by Redwood. That preserves continuity for your jobs while protecting Redwood's ability to reassign GPUs.
- We can add a clause referencing SOC 2 audit support and where evidence will be shared (secure S3 link with role-based access).

I copied Marcus for legal language and Laura for billing implications (the reduced reserved rate and how it will appear on invoices). Marcus — can you draft redline text for the three bullets above by EOD?

I’ll book a 30-minute call tomorrow at 2:00pm PST unless you prefer a different time.

Jordan
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@swiftframe.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-15T08:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync

Team / Elena —

I reviewed the requested changes and attached a redline (SwiftFrame_CoverageSchedule_redline_v2.pdf) and a Track Changes MSA amendment (Redwood_MSA_amendment_track_changes.docx). Summary of legal positions:

1) Retention window: we can agree to a 30-day retention limit for cached inference artifacts but need to add narrow language excluding telemetry and core system logs (those remain at 90 days for compliance). Proposed snippet: "Customer KV/cache artifacts subject to retention of no more than thirty (30) days; activity logs and system telemetry remain within Redwood's standard retention schedule."

2) Scale-down notice & grace: propose 14-day written notice OR immediate scale-down with payment for a one-week grace period at the reduced reserved rate (attached formula). This gives SwiftFrame the 14-day operational window while protecting Redwood.

3) SOC2 / audit access: propose an addendum paragraph that specifies the mechanism (time-bound presigned URLs or secure portal), frequency, and redaction process for PII. We will not change the Master Agreement's core audit exclusions, but will provide operational evidence where permissible.

Open items for negotiation: final definition of "cached inference artifacts" (we added a definition that ties to object prefixes and retention TTL) and invoicing cadence for grace-period charges. Laura to confirm billing treatment.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SwiftFrame_CoverageSchedule_redline_v2.pdf, Redwood_MSA_amendment_track_changes.docx
From: Elena Rossi <elena@swiftframe.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@swiftframe.com>
Date: 2027-11-15T10:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync

Marcus —

Thanks for the clean redline. A couple of quick asks on wording: 
- Please expand the KV/cache artifacts definition to explicitly include model session output and temporary inference logs (these are the items our auditors flagged).
- For the SOC2 access, can Redwood commit to a 10-business-day turnaround on requested evidence during an audit window?

If you can add those two clarifications I think we're close. I'll also route the updated redline to procurement for pricing confirmation.

If Jordan can send the DocuSign package with the tracked changes attached after we finalize wording, procurement will push to signatures next week.

Elena
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@swiftframe.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-16T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coverage schedule & MSA addendum — redline sync

Elena —

Great — Marcus will incorporate the expanded KV/cache definition and the 10-business-day audit evidence SLA into v3 of the redline by COB today. Laura and I confirmed the billing path: the one-week grace buffer will be billed on the next invoice under "Reserved Capacity Adjustments" and will appear as a prorated line item; no separate SOW required.

I created the DocuSign envelope (link below) and will not send until we have Marcus's v3. Planned next steps:
- Marcus: v3 redline with definitions + audit SLA (COB today)
- Jordan: load v3 into DocuSign, send to Elena + Alex for signature
- Procurement: sign and close — target signature by 2027-11-23
